section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses managerial implications derived from a study on salesperson adaptation to change. It highlights that goal orientations (specifically low Performance Orientation and high Learning Orientation) are important predictors for learning-related changes, while experience is not. Managers are advised to consider redefining performance metrics during periods of change to include implementation behaviors like technology use, in addition to sales quotas, to facilitate adaptation among high-PO employees.

section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses managerial implications regarding determinants of salesperson adaptation to change. It highlights that goal orientations (LO and PO) are important for learning-related change, while experience is not. The study suggests that managers should consider redefining performance metrics during periods of change to include implementation behaviors in addition to sales, especially for high-PO employees. Table 4 presents cross-sectional multiple regression results showing standardized coefficients for various predictors (OC, USE, EXP, LO, PO) on performance at different time points (t=0 to t=11).
